reasons.specificity: It sharply distinguishes the 2001 entrepreneurship-and-myth mechanism from the 2022 world-society, self-description, and unbounded-markets argument.
reasons.anchoring: Nearly all quotations occur and support the stated readings, though F3 treats Deutschmann’s interpretive phrase “option to have options” somewhat loosely as an explicitly Simmelian concept.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully isolates the subsistence condition, the shift from cyclical myths to continuing imaginations, and moral minimalism as a limit on capitalism–religion equivalence.
reasons.coherence: The prose, source-use table, transmission table, and findings consistently present conceptual adaptation while withholding any claim of demonstrated direct borrowing.
reasons.usefulness: The two main tables directly answer the requested inventory and foreground gains and losses, but extensive duplicated ledgers and scope-review material reduce desk usability.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Claims are generally bounded to the supplied texts and the absence of a 2022 cross-citation is handled cautiously, with no major invented contradiction, consensus, or transmission link.

score.one_line: A highly source-specific and well-anchored adaptation inventory whose main weakness is excessive duplication rather than substantive error.
